newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 15.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on November 15. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Indonesia's Attorney General has received information on problematic non-governmental organisations, a spokesman said. It is now checking the information to see whether the aims of these NGOs are in line with state ideology.

Indonesian Vice President Try Sutrisno called on the country's career women not to forget their duties in the household. Health minister Sujudi said that 37 million women currently work, compared to 16.9 million in 1988.

Hasan Basri, head of the influential Moslem Council of Ulemas, said that the recent row over comments made by Nobel laureate Bishop Belo about Indonesian treatement of East Timorese was not a religious problem.

Automotive components makers reported that during the first half of 1996, total production of automotive components reached $717.4 million. They predicted that by the end of 1996, components will achieve earnings of $1.42 billion, an increase of about 22 percent against total value in 1995.
